Vulnerabilities.Title: brotli: Out-of-Bounds Write in Google Brotli Decoder
Vulnerabilities.Description:
A buffer overflow vulnerability in the Brotli decoder (c/dec/decode.c) in Google Brotli versions 1.0.3 through 1.2.0 on all platforms allows a remote unauthenticated attacker to corrupt adjacent decoder state memory, disclose sensitive memory contents, cause a denial of service, or potentially execute arbitrary code using a crafted Brotli-compressed stream.





Users need to update any Brotli libraries or binaries between 1.0.3 through 1.2.0 to the latest available version: 1.0.10 or 1.1.1 or 1.2.1.

Vulnerabilities.Title: curl: curl: HTTP/2 upload Use-After-Free
Vulnerabilities.Description:
During an upload, curl mishandles HTTP/2 `RST_STREAM` received from the server
(with reason `HTTP_1_1_REQUIRED` or `REFUSED_STREAM`) leading to a use after
free of a `struct Curl_easy` object.

Vulnerabilities.Title: curl: curl: FTP wildcard write callback mixup
Vulnerabilities.Description:
When an FTP wildcard `LIST` operation fails, libcurl omits the restoration
path meant for successful listings, leaving the write callback set to the
internal listing parser and the write callback data pointing directly to the
easy handle. Subsequent reuse of this handle triggers an immediate crash, and
cloning it via `curl_easy_duphandle()` copies this corrupted state into the
duplicate. If the original handle is subsequently freed, executing a transfer
on the cloned handle causes a heap use-after-free read against the dangling
handle reference; alternatively, reusing the original or cloned handle while
changing only  `CURLOPT_WRITEDATA` (and omitting `CURLOPT_WRITEFUNCTION`)
results in type confusion, forcing the internal parser to interpret incoming
server response bytes into memory at the application-supplied write data
pointer.

Vulnerabilities.Title: curl: curl: info leak uploading over WebSockets with GnuTLS
Vulnerabilities.Description:
When curl is built with GnuTLS, a malicious WebSocket server can make curl
send memory past its send buffer. This is due to an out of bounds read
following when `gnutls_record_send()` returns a number of bytes sent **greater
than the number of bytes it was given to send**. GnuTLS does that after a
blocked send.

Vulnerabilities.Title: curl: curl: local interface connection reuse mixup
Vulnerabilities.Description:
When `CURLOPT_INTERFACE` (or the command line tool's `--interface` option) is
set with one of the documented prefixes (`if!`, `host!`, `ifhost!`), that
binding is not part of the connection reuse key, so a later transfer asking
for a different source can silently reuse an existing connection and go out
from the earlier transfer's source address

Vulnerabilities.Title: curl: curl: stale SigV4 headers sent unintended
Vulnerabilities.Description:
Setting `CURLOPT_AWS_SIGV4` to NULL but does not disable SigV4 authentication,
contrary to expectations and documentation. A subsequent transfer on the same
handle still sends an `Authorization: AWS4-HMAC-SHA256` header to whatever URL
isset next, leaking state information.

Vulnerabilities.Title: curl: curl: redirect to SFTP or SCP bypasses host verification
Vulnerabilities.Description:
A flaw in the curl command line tool's logic makes it only set SSH host
verification options when interacting directly using SFTP or SCP, and not as a
result of following a redirect.

Vulnerabilities.Title: curl: curl: FTP connection reuse inherits client-certificate
Vulnerabilities.Description:
An `ftp://` transfer configured with `CURLUSESSL_NONE` can reuse a pooled FTP
control connection that a previous easy handle upgraded with `STARTTLS` and
authenticated using a client certificate. The second handle performs neither a
new TLS handshake nor a new FTP login, so the server continues to authorize it
under the first handle's certificate identity.

Vulnerabilities.Title: curl: curl: server-set cookie erases cookie jar
Vulnerabilities.Description:
A remote HTTP server can set a cookie that curl accepts and writes to a
Netscape cookie jar but cannot reload. On the next invocation using the same
path for `--cookie` and `--cookie-jar`, curl fails before connecting, then the
cleanup procedure replaces the jar with an empty file, deleting cookies for
unrelated domains.

Vulnerabilities.Title: curl: curl: Negotiate credentials sent to redirected origin
Vulnerabilities.Description:
When using an *ambient user* in a first transfer doing Negotiate
authentication and asked to follow redirects, curl could pass on its
credential details to an unrelated second origin when asked to redirect there.

Vulnerabilities.Title: curl: curl: leaking host credentials to HTTP proxy
Vulnerabilities.Description:
An HTTP proxy can trick libcurl into sending the origin's credentials (Basic
password, or a Negotiate/Kerberos ticket) to the proxy itself, by answering
the `CONNECT` tunnel request with 401 `WWW-Authenticate:` instead of the
expected 407 `Proxy-Authenticate:`.

Vulnerabilities.Title: curl: curl: auto client cert connection reuse mixup
Vulnerabilities.Description:
libcurl's connection cache match function never considers the automatic client
certificate option, so a cached, already authenticated Schannel connection can
be handed to a transfer that got redirected to a different origin, even though
the code explicitly switched off the auto client cert option for that transfer
to prevent exactly this.

Vulnerabilities.Title: curl: curl: cross-origin reuse of a Negotiate connection
Vulnerabilities.Description:
When using ambient user credentials, an HTTP request directed to one origin
may be dispatched over a connection previously authenticated via Negotiate for
a different origin, leaving the request's intended credentials unused.

Vulnerabilities.Title: curl: curl: HSTS cache import drops longer-lived child
Vulnerabilities.Description:
Importing a `includeSubDomains` parent HSTS entry before a longer-lived child
entry, silently drops the child. Consequently, when the parent expires, the
child's valid HSTS policy is lost, causing curl to issue unencrypted HTTP
requests rather than upgrading to HTTPS.

Vulnerabilities.Title: curl: curl: Hsts Response Erases Persisted Entries
Vulnerabilities.Description:
An authenticated HTTPS origin can supply an HSTS `max-age` value that the
parser accepts, but time serialization later fails to process. On 64-bit
systems, extreme max-age values compute an absolute expiry within standard
time integer limits that exceeds calendar time structure bounds. During cache
saves, the original HSTS file is truncated before writing a temporary
replacement; when serialization fails, the temporary file is deleted, leaving
an empty or partial cache. Because the save error is silently ignored during
cleanup, curl exits successfully despite the data loss.

Vulnerabilities.Title: curl: IMAP APPEND plus CRLF conversion command injection
Vulnerabilities.Description:
Enabling `CURLOPT_CRLF` causes curl to advertise the raw input byte count in
the `IMAP APPEND {N}` literal while transmitting line-ending expanded data.
The server reads only $N$ bytes for the payload, causing the remaining
overflow bytes to be interpreted and executed as pipelined IMAP commands
within the authenticated session.

Vulnerabilities.Title: curl: curl: knownhost callback mismatches key as missing
Vulnerabilities.Description:
When libcurl uses libssh2 with a hashed `known_hosts` file, an unrelated
initial entry can cause host key validation to report a key *mismatch* as a
*missing* key to the `CURLOPT_SSH_KEYFUNCTION` callback.

Vulnerabilities.Title: curl: curl: wolfSSL public-key pinning bypass
Vulnerabilities.Description:
When built with wolfSSL, curl can successfully validate a pinned public key
hash against a key the TLS peer does not possess. During the TLS handshake,
wolfSSL validates the connection, but curl's subsequent re-parsing of the same
certificate - tricked by a manipulated validity length field - extracts and
matches a different embedded key, incorrectly authorizing the pinned public
key.

Vulnerabilities.Title: curl: curl: server-set cookie aborts cookie jar load
Vulnerabilities.Description:
When writing a long cookie name and value to a Netscape cookie jar, a remote
HTTP server can make `curl` write a record that exceeds its line-length
parsing limit. Consequently, any subsequent `curl` invocation reading from
that same cookie jar using `--cookie` silently aborts parsing prematurely upon
encountering the too long line, ignoring all subsequent valid cookies in the
file.

Vulnerabilities.Title: curl: curl: never-ending loop via server response omission
Vulnerabilities.Description:
By permanently omitting the final control-response line, a malicious FTP,
IMAP, POP3, or SMTP server can exploit libcurl and completely bypass its
configured transfer timeout mechanism, indefinitely blocking all concurrent
transfers bound to the same multi-handle.

Vulnerabilities.Title: curl: curl: TFTP direction confusion
Vulnerabilities.Description:
libcurl's TFTP state machine fails to validate state transitions against the
requested transfer direction, accepting opening server responses for both
reads and writes interchangeably. A malicious TFTP server can respond to a
download request in a way that forces the client into transmit mode, prompting
libcurl to consume and transmit data from the handle's persistent
`CURLOPT_READDATA` pointer - including data remaining from unrelated prior
operations, such as an HTTP POST request executed on a reused handle.

Vulnerabilities.Title: curl: curl: -J no-clobber guarantee bypassed with 103 early hints
Vulnerabilities.Description:
When invoked with `--remote-header-name` (`-J`), curl fails to preserve its
documented anti-clobbering protection if an intermediate 103 Early Hints
response precedes the final HTTP response, or if an `ETag` header is processed
before `Content-Disposition` under `--etag-save`. This flaw allows an HTTP(S)
server to overwrite an existing local file specified in the
`Content-Disposition` header despite the presence of the `-J` non-overwrite
constraint.

Vulnerabilities.Title: curl: curl: curl_mime_free stack overflow by recursion
Vulnerabilities.Description:
A deeply nested multipart MIME structure constructed via the public API causes
a stack overflow in libcurl during normal cleanup operations. An excessive
recursion depth within `curl_mime_free` leads to unbounded stack frame
allocation during structure traversal, ultimately crashing the host process.

Vulnerabilities.Title: curl: curl: Authorization: Negotiate sent to foreign origin
Vulnerabilities.Description:
When processing an HTTP redirect to a URL containing userinfo (a
`username:password` component), curl might erroneously retain and re-transmit
the original host's HTTP Negotiate authentication state. Consequently, a
malicious server can trigger a redirect containing arbitrary userinfo to force
curl to send a freshly minted Kerberos ticket—generated using the ambient
identity of the client process to an untrusted third-party host, effectively
bypassing the domain-scoping restrictions normally enforced by the absence of
`--location-trusted`.

Vulnerabilities.Title: curl: curl: password leak in CURLINFO_EFFECTIVE_URL
Vulnerabilities.Description:
libcurl could accidentally return a URL for `curl_easy_getinfo()`'s
`CURLINFO_EFFECTIVE_URL` option containing credentials, even though neither
the URL provided to libcurl nor the redirected URL did.

Vulnerabilities.Title: Issue summary: Encrypting a CMS message to an EC certificate whose gro ...
Vulnerabilities.Description:
Issue summary: Encrypting a CMS message to an EC certificate whose group order
is 1 may cause CMS_encrypt() or CMS_encrypt_ex() to loop indefinitely.

Impact summary: An attacker able to supply the recipient certificate to an
application performing CMS encryption can cause that application to loop
indefinitely, consuming CPU and resulting in Denial of Service.

CWE: CWE-835: Loop with Unreachable Exit Condition ('Infinite Loop')

Description: CMS_encrypt() and CMS_encrypt_ex() encrypt a message to one or
more recipient certificates and, for an EC recipient, generate an ephemeral
key in the recipient's group. If the certificate declares a group order of 1,
random scalar generation can only produce zero. The key generation routine
then retries without limit while waiting for a nonzero private scalar, so the
call never returns.

The OpenSSL TLS and QUIC implementations do not use this path. An application
is exposed only if it calls CMS_encrypt() or CMS_encrypt_ex() with a recipient
certificate whose EC parameters are attacker-controlled. Certificates with
normal EC group orders do not trigger the loop.

OpenSSL 4.0 and later reject unknown explicit EC groups in default builds.
These versions are affected only when configured with the
enable-ec_explicit_curves option.

The result is a hang that consumes a CPU core until the process is
interrupted, a Denial of Service. The severity is Low because the attacker
must supply the recipient certificate and the application must choose to
encrypt to it; ordinary CMS encryption to trusted recipients is unaffected.

The fix makes EC key generation fail when the group has no valid nonzero
private scalar, instead of retrying indefinitely.

FIPS impact: no
The FIPS modules in 4.1, 4.0, 3.5 and 3.0 are not affected. The FIPS provider
does not support arbitrary explicit EC domain parameters, so an order-1 group
is rejected during key import before the vulnerable key generation path is
reached.

Vulnerabilities.Title: Issue summary: QUIC, when performing automated peer detection, may all ...
Vulnerabilities.Description:
Issue summary: QUIC, when performing automated peer detection, may allow
uninitialized stack data to leak into the received address which is then used
as the destination for outgoing packets.

Impact summary: Applications using QUIC's automated peer detection mechanism
may receive an invalid address, leading to connection loss and disclosure of
uninitialized stack data to an attacker observing the outgoing network traffic.

CWE: CWE-457 (Use of Uninitialized Variable)

Description: The OpenSSL QUIC stack contains a feature in which, when using an
already connected socket, it will auto-detect the peer address during the SSL
handshake.  This feature uses the getpeername() function, passing a buffer of
sufficient length to hold any supported address family, but passes a buffer
length that is only sized such that larger addresses, such as IPv6, cannot be
retrieved. The getpeername() function however, still returns the full address
length, which is accepted as the valid input buffer length, leading to the
address buffer containing uninitialized stack data instead of the actual peer
address. The invalid peer address is then used as destination for the outgoing
packets which leads to a connectivity breakage and a leakage of the
uninitialized stack data to passive network observers.

FIPS impact: no
The FIPS modules in 4.0, 3.6, 3.5, 3.4, and 3.0 are not affected by this CVE as
the affected protocol is not implemented in the FIPS module.

Vulnerabilities.Title: Issue summary: The AES-GCM-SIV implementation treats a zero-length Add ...
Vulnerabilities.Description:
Issue summary: The AES-GCM-SIV implementation treats a zero-length Additional
Authenticated Data (AAD) update as a reset of all the AAD supplied so far,
instead of leaving the AAD unchanged. An application that supplies its AAD in
several fragments, one of which is empty, therefore produces or verifies
messages whose authentication tag does not cover the AAD supplied before
the empty fragment.

Impact summary: Data an application intended to authenticate alongside a
message is silently left unauthenticated. An attacker can forge the AAD of such
a message.

CWE: CWE-325: Missing Cryptographic Step

Description: An application passing AAD in multiple chunks of which some have
zero length will have the previous AAD chunks effectively unauthenticated. Also,
on context re-initialisation, the AAD was not reset, which meant that any AAD
accumulated from the previous context usage were also included in the AAD of the
new message.

The fix makes a zero-length AAD update a no-op and clears any accumulated AAD
whenever the context is re-initialised with a key or a nonce.
A re-initialisation that only changes parameters keeps the AAD.

FIPS impact: no
The FIPS modules are not affected, as AES-GCM-SIV is not a FIPS approved
algorithm and is implemented only in the default provider, outside the
OpenSSL FIPS module boundary.

Vulnerabilities.Title: Issue summary: A retransmitted QUIC CRYPTO frame can release packet st ...
Vulnerabilities.Description:
Issue summary: A retransmitted QUIC CRYPTO frame can release packet storage
while the TLS record layer retains a direct pointer into that storage causing
use after free.

Impact summary: A malicious QUIC server can cause a heap-use-after-free read
in the OpenSSL QUIC client. The server can also identify one allocator-adjacent
byte through the client's protected Handshake response.

CWE: CWE-416: Use After Free

Description: During CRYPTO stream processing, a pointer into the first frame's
memory on the stream is lent to the TLS handshake processing. The memory
must remain stable until it is processed and released. However the processing
of retransmitted CRYPTO frames could release the memory if the retransmitted
frame fully overlapped the existing frame. This then causes use-after-free read
when the TLS handshake processing continues.

The use-after-free read can lead to a Denial-of-Service of the client
application or a minor leak of information about the heap memory contents
that might be overwritten with other data, subsequently allocated by
the application, to the peer.

FIPS impact: no
The FIPS module is not affected as the QUIC implementation is outside of
the OpenSSL FIPS module boundary.

Vulnerabilities.Title: Issue summary: Setting an AES-GCM-SIV IV shorter than the expected non ...
Vulnerabilities.Description:
Issue summary: Setting an AES-GCM-SIV IV shorter than the expected nonce
length via EVP_CipherInit_ex() may trigger a heap out-of-bounds read.
Supplying a longer IV is silently truncated instead of rejected.

Impact summary: An application passing a caller-supplied IV of the wrong
length may crash or read beyond its buffer. Because trailing IV bytes are
ignored, an attacker who knows one message and tag may forge messages under a
different IV.

CWE: CWE-125: Out-of-bounds Read

Description: AES-GCM-SIV copies the caller-supplied IV or nonce into its
internal state using a copy whose length is taken from the expected nonce size
rather than from the length the caller actually provided. When the caller
passes a shorter IV, the copy reads past the end of the caller's buffer;
AddressSanitizer confirms a heap out-of-bounds read reached through
EVP_CipherInit_ex() into ossl_aes_gcm_siv_init(). When the caller passes a
longer IV, the implementation silently discards the trailing bytes instead of
rejecting the length.

The truncation breaks the binding between the IV and the computed
authentication tag. An attacker who has observed a message and its tag under
one IV can produce a message and tag that verify under a different IV whose
first bytes match, since the surplus bytes never influence the computation.
The message itself is unchanged, so this is a failure of IV commitment rather
than a classic existential forgery.

Only applications that call EVP_CipherInit_ex() (or the equivalent provider
cipher initialization) with an IV length other than the standard 12 bytes for
AES-GCM-SIV are affected. The severity is limited because the out-of-bounds
read is small and attacker-controlled only in length, and the forgery requires
an unusual IV length choice by the application.

FIPS impact: no
The FIPS modules are not affected by this issue, as AES-GCM-SIV is not an
approved algorithm.

under the first handle's certificate identity.

Vulnerabilities.Title: curl: curl: server-set cookie erases cookie jar
Vulnerabilities.Description:
A remote HTTP server can set a cookie that curl accepts and writes to a
Netscape cookie jar but cannot reload. On the next invocation using the same
path for `--cookie` and `--cookie-jar`, curl fails before connecting, then the
cleanup procedure replaces the jar with an empty file, deleting cookies for
unrelated domains.

Vulnerabilities.Title: curl: curl: Negotiate credentials sent to redirected origin
Vulnerabilities.Description:
When using an *ambient user* in a first transfer doing Negotiate
authentication and asked to follow redirects, curl could pass on its
credential details to an unrelated second origin when asked to redirect there.

Vulnerabilities.Title: curl: curl: leaking host credentials to HTTP proxy
Vulnerabilities.Description:
An HTTP proxy can trick libcurl into sending the origin's credentials (Basic
password, or a Negotiate/Kerberos ticket) to the proxy itself, by answering
the `CONNECT` tunnel request with 401 `WWW-Authenticate:` instead of the
expected 407 `Proxy-Authenticate:`.

Vulnerabilities.Title: curl: curl: auto client cert connection reuse mixup
Vulnerabilities.Description:
libcurl's connection cache match function never considers the automatic client
certificate option, so a cached, already authenticated Schannel connection can
be handed to a transfer that got redirected to a different origin, even though
the code explicitly switched off the auto client cert option for that transfer
to prevent exactly this.

Vulnerabilities.Title: curl: curl: cross-origin reuse of a Negotiate connection
Vulnerabilities.Description:
When using ambient user credentials, an HTTP request directed to one origin
may be dispatched over a connection previously authenticated via Negotiate for
a different origin, leaving the request's intended credentials unused.

Vulnerabilities.Title: curl: curl: HSTS cache import drops longer-lived child
Vulnerabilities.Description:
Importing a `includeSubDomains` parent HSTS entry before a longer-lived child
entry, silently drops the child. Consequently, when the parent expires, the
child's valid HSTS policy is lost, causing curl to issue unencrypted HTTP
requests rather than upgrading to HTTPS.

Vulnerabilities.Title: curl: curl: Hsts Response Erases Persisted Entries
Vulnerabilities.Description:
An authenticated HTTPS origin can supply an HSTS `max-age` value that the
parser accepts, but time serialization later fails to process. On 64-bit
systems, extreme max-age values compute an absolute expiry within standard
time integer limits that exceeds calendar time structure bounds. During cache
saves, the original HSTS file is truncated before writing a temporary
replacement; when serialization fails, the temporary file is deleted, leaving
an empty or partial cache. Because the save error is silently ignored during
cleanup, curl exits successfully despite the data loss.

Vulnerabilities.Title: curl: IMAP APPEND plus CRLF conversion command injection
Vulnerabilities.Description:
Enabling `CURLOPT_CRLF` causes curl to advertise the raw input byte count in
the `IMAP APPEND {N}` literal while transmitting line-ending expanded data.
The server reads only $N$ bytes for the payload, causing the remaining
overflow bytes to be interpreted and executed as pipelined IMAP commands
within the authenticated session.

Vulnerabilities.Title: curl: curl: knownhost callback mismatches key as missing
Vulnerabilities.Description:
When libcurl uses libssh2 with a hashed `known_hosts` file, an unrelated
initial entry can cause host key validation to report a key *mismatch* as a
*missing* key to the `CURLOPT_SSH_KEYFUNCTION` callback.

Vulnerabilities.Title: curl: curl: wolfSSL public-key pinning bypass
Vulnerabilities.Description:
When built with wolfSSL, curl can successfully validate a pinned public key
hash against a key the TLS peer does not possess. During the TLS handshake,
wolfSSL validates the connection, but curl's subsequent re-parsing of the same
certificate - tricked by a manipulated validity length field - extracts and
matches a different embedded key, incorrectly authorizing the pinned public
key.

Vulnerabilities.Title: curl: curl: server-set cookie aborts cookie jar load
Vulnerabilities.Description:
When writing a long cookie name and value to a Netscape cookie jar, a remote
HTTP server can make `curl` write a record that exceeds its line-length
parsing limit. Consequently, any subsequent `curl` invocation reading from
that same cookie jar using `--cookie` silently aborts parsing prematurely upon
encountering the too long line, ignoring all subsequent valid cookies in the
file.

Vulnerabilities.Title: curl: curl: never-ending loop via server response omission
Vulnerabilities.Description:
By permanently omitting the final control-response line, a malicious FTP,
IMAP, POP3, or SMTP server can exploit libcurl and completely bypass its
configured transfer timeout mechanism, indefinitely blocking all concurrent
transfers bound to the same multi-handle.

Vulnerabilities.Title: curl: curl: TFTP direction confusion
Vulnerabilities.Description:
libcurl's TFTP state machine fails to validate state transitions against the
requested transfer direction, accepting opening server responses for both
reads and writes interchangeably. A malicious TFTP server can respond to a
download request in a way that forces the client into transmit mode, prompting
libcurl to consume and transmit data from the handle's persistent
`CURLOPT_READDATA` pointer - including data remaining from unrelated prior
operations, such as an HTTP POST request executed on a reused handle.

Vulnerabilities.Title: curl: curl: -J no-clobber guarantee bypassed with 103 early hints
Vulnerabilities.Description:
When invoked with `--remote-header-name` (`-J`), curl fails to preserve its
documented anti-clobbering protection if an intermediate 103 Early Hints
response precedes the final HTTP response, or if an `ETag` header is processed
before `Content-Disposition` under `--etag-save`. This flaw allows an HTTP(S)
server to overwrite an existing local file specified in the
`Content-Disposition` header despite the presence of the `-J` non-overwrite
constraint.

Vulnerabilities.Title: curl: curl: curl_mime_free stack overflow by recursion
Vulnerabilities.Description:
A deeply nested multipart MIME structure constructed via the public API causes
a stack overflow in libcurl during normal cleanup operations. An excessive
recursion depth within `curl_mime_free` leads to unbounded stack frame
allocation during structure traversal, ultimately crashing the host process.

Vulnerabilities.Title: curl: curl: Authorization: Negotiate sent to foreign origin
Vulnerabilities.Description:
When processing an HTTP redirect to a URL containing userinfo (a
`username:password` component), curl might erroneously retain and re-transmit
the original host's HTTP Negotiate authentication state. Consequently, a
malicious server can trigger a redirect containing arbitrary userinfo to force
curl to send a freshly minted Kerberos ticket—generated using the ambient
identity of the client process to an untrusted third-party host, effectively
bypassing the domain-scoping restrictions normally enforced by the absence of
`--location-trusted`.

Vulnerabilities.Title: curl: curl: password leak in CURLINFO_EFFECTIVE_URL
Vulnerabilities.Description:
libcurl could accidentally return a URL for `curl_easy_getinfo()`'s
`CURLINFO_EFFECTIVE_URL` option containing credentials, even though neither
the URL provided to libcurl nor the redirected URL did.

Vulnerabilities.Title: expat: expat: Denial of Service via improper memory tracking in XML_ParserReset
Vulnerabilities.Description: libexpat 2.7.2 through 2.9.0 contains a denial of service vulnerability because XML_ParserReset zeroes the direct byte count but never offsets tracked heap allocations. Attackers can submit a large XML document so later documents on the same reset parser fail with XML_ERROR_NO_MEMORY until it is recreated.

Vulnerabilities.Title: expat: expat: Denial of Service via delayed entity amplification detection
Vulnerabilities.Description: libexpat through 2.9.0 contains a denial of service vulnerability because billion laughs protection in accountingDiffTolerated() in xmlparse.c detects entity amplification too late. Attackers can supply a moderately sized XML document with a large DTD and nested entity expansions to consume tens of seconds of CPU per parse.

Vulnerabilities.Title: expat: expat: Denial of Service via NULL pointer dereference in external entity parsing
Vulnerabilities.Description: libexpat through 2.9.0 contains a NULL pointer dereference vulnerability in externalEntityInitProcessor2() in lib/xmlparse.c that mishandles the XML_TOK_NONE token from empty input. Attackers who control stream chunking can force an empty non-final first parse on an external entity subparser, causing a later parse to crash the application.

Vulnerabilities.Title: expat: expat: Denial of Service via integer overflow during XML attribute parsing
Vulnerabilities.Description: libexpat through 2.9.0 contains a signed integer overflow vulnerability in storeAtts() in lib/xmlparse.c that allows attackers to trigger out-of-bounds writes via oversized attribute counts. Attackers can supply a multi-gigabyte document with a start tag carrying over 2^30 attributes to overflow attIndex and nPrefixes, crashing applications or corrupting heap memory.

Vulnerabilities.Title: Issue summary: Encrypting a CMS message to an EC certificate whose gro ...
Vulnerabilities.Description:
Issue summary: Encrypting a CMS message to an EC certificate whose group order
is 1 may cause CMS_encrypt() or CMS_encrypt_ex() to loop indefinitely.

Impact summary: An attacker able to supply the recipient certificate to an
application performing CMS encryption can cause that application to loop
indefinitely, consuming CPU and resulting in Denial of Service.

CWE: CWE-835: Loop with Unreachable Exit Condition ('Infinite Loop')

Description: CMS_encrypt() and CMS_encrypt_ex() encrypt a message to one or
more recipient certificates and, for an EC recipient, generate an ephemeral
key in the recipient's group. If the certificate declares a group order of 1,
random scalar generation can only produce zero. The key generation routine
then retries without limit while waiting for a nonzero private scalar, so the
call never returns.

The OpenSSL TLS and QUIC implementations do not use this path. An application
is exposed only if it calls CMS_encrypt() or CMS_encrypt_ex() with a recipient
certificate whose EC parameters are attacker-controlled. Certificates with
normal EC group orders do not trigger the loop.

OpenSSL 4.0 and later reject unknown explicit EC groups in default builds.
These versions are affected only when configured with the
enable-ec_explicit_curves option.

The result is a hang that consumes a CPU core until the process is
interrupted, a Denial of Service. The severity is Low because the attacker
must supply the recipient certificate and the application must choose to
encrypt to it; ordinary CMS encryption to trusted recipients is unaffected.

The fix makes EC key generation fail when the group has no valid nonzero
private scalar, instead of retrying indefinitely.

FIPS impact: no
The FIPS modules in 4.1, 4.0, 3.5 and 3.0 are not affected. The FIPS provider
does not support arbitrary explicit EC domain parameters, so an order-1 group
is rejected during key import before the vulnerable key generation path is
reached.

Vulnerabilities.Title: Issue summary: QUIC, when performing automated peer detection, may all ...
Vulnerabilities.Description:
Issue summary: QUIC, when performing automated peer detection, may allow
uninitialized stack data to leak into the received address which is then used
as the destination for outgoing packets.

Impact summary: Applications using QUIC's automated peer detection mechanism
may receive an invalid address, leading to connection loss and disclosure of
uninitialized stack data to an attacker observing the outgoing network traffic.

CWE: CWE-457 (Use of Uninitialized Variable)

Description: The OpenSSL QUIC stack contains a feature in which, when using an
already connected socket, it will auto-detect the peer address during the SSL
handshake.  This feature uses the getpeername() function, passing a buffer of
sufficient length to hold any supported address family, but passes a buffer
length that is only sized such that larger addresses, such as IPv6, cannot be
retrieved. The getpeername() function however, still returns the full address
length, which is accepted as the valid input buffer length, leading to the
address buffer containing uninitialized stack data instead of the actual peer
address. The invalid peer address is then used as destination for the outgoing
packets which leads to a connectivity breakage and a leakage of the
uninitialized stack data to passive network observers.

FIPS impact: no
The FIPS modules in 4.0, 3.6, 3.5, 3.4, and 3.0 are not affected by this CVE as
the affected protocol is not implemented in the FIPS module.

Vulnerabilities.Title: Issue summary: The AES-GCM-SIV implementation treats a zero-length Add ...
Vulnerabilities.Description:
Issue summary: The AES-GCM-SIV implementation treats a zero-length Additional
Authenticated Data (AAD) update as a reset of all the AAD supplied so far,
instead of leaving the AAD unchanged. An application that supplies its AAD in
several fragments, one of which is empty, therefore produces or verifies
messages whose authentication tag does not cover the AAD supplied before
the empty fragment.

Impact summary: Data an application intended to authenticate alongside a
message is silently left unauthenticated. An attacker can forge the AAD of such
a message.

CWE: CWE-325: Missing Cryptographic Step

Description: An application passing AAD in multiple chunks of which some have
zero length will have the previous AAD chunks effectively unauthenticated. Also,
on context re-initialisation, the AAD was not reset, which meant that any AAD
accumulated from the previous context usage were also included in the AAD of the
new message.

The fix makes a zero-length AAD update a no-op and clears any accumulated AAD
whenever the context is re-initialised with a key or a nonce.
A re-initialisation that only changes parameters keeps the AAD.

FIPS impact: no
The FIPS modules are not affected, as AES-GCM-SIV is not a FIPS approved
algorithm and is implemented only in the default provider, outside the
OpenSSL FIPS module boundary.

Vulnerabilities.Title: Issue summary: A retransmitted QUIC CRYPTO frame can release packet st ...
Vulnerabilities.Description:
Issue summary: A retransmitted QUIC CRYPTO frame can release packet storage
while the TLS record layer retains a direct pointer into that storage causing
use after free.

Impact summary: A malicious QUIC server can cause a heap-use-after-free read
in the OpenSSL QUIC client. The server can also identify one allocator-adjacent
byte through the client's protected Handshake response.

CWE: CWE-416: Use After Free

Description: During CRYPTO stream processing, a pointer into the first frame's
memory on the stream is lent to the TLS handshake processing. The memory
must remain stable until it is processed and released. However the processing
of retransmitted CRYPTO frames could release the memory if the retransmitted
frame fully overlapped the existing frame. This then causes use-after-free read
when the TLS handshake processing continues.

The use-after-free read can lead to a Denial-of-Service of the client
application or a minor leak of information about the heap memory contents
that might be overwritten with other data, subsequently allocated by
the application, to the peer.

FIPS impact: no
The FIPS module is not affected as the QUIC implementation is outside of
the OpenSSL FIPS module boundary.

Vulnerabilities.Title: Issue summary: Setting an AES-GCM-SIV IV shorter than the expected non ...
Vulnerabilities.Description:
Issue summary: Setting an AES-GCM-SIV IV shorter than the expected nonce
length via EVP_CipherInit_ex() may trigger a heap out-of-bounds read.
Supplying a longer IV is silently truncated instead of rejected.

Impact summary: An application passing a caller-supplied IV of the wrong
length may crash or read beyond its buffer. Because trailing IV bytes are
ignored, an attacker who knows one message and tag may forge messages under a
different IV.

CWE: CWE-125: Out-of-bounds Read

Description: AES-GCM-SIV copies the caller-supplied IV or nonce into its
internal state using a copy whose length is taken from the expected nonce size
rather than from the length the caller actually provided. When the caller
passes a shorter IV, the copy reads past the end of the caller's buffer;
AddressSanitizer confirms a heap out-of-bounds read reached through
EVP_CipherInit_ex() into ossl_aes_gcm_siv_init(). When the caller passes a
longer IV, the implementation silently discards the trailing bytes instead of
rejecting the length.

The truncation breaks the binding between the IV and the computed
authentication tag. An attacker who has observed a message and its tag under
one IV can produce a message and tag that verify under a different IV whose
first bytes match, since the surplus bytes never influence the computation.
The message itself is unchanged, so this is a failure of IV commitment rather
than a classic existential forgery.

Only applications that call EVP_CipherInit_ex() (or the equivalent provider
cipher initialization) with an IV length other than the standard 12 bytes for
AES-GCM-SIV are affected. The severity is limited because the out-of-bounds
read is small and attacker-controlled only in length, and the forgery requires
an unusual IV length choice by the application.

FIPS impact: no
The FIPS modules are not affected by this issue, as AES-GCM-SIV is not an
approved algorithm.

Vulnerabilities.Title: chromium-browser: Use after free in XML
Vulnerabilities.Description: Use after free in XML in Google Chrome prior to 157.0.8103.50 allowed a remote attacker to execute arbitrary code inside the sandbox via a crafted HTML page. (Chromium security severity: High)

Vulnerabilities.Title: chromium-browser: chromium-browser: Type confusion in XML
Vulnerabilities.Description: Type confusion in XML in Google Chrome prior to 153.0.8010.36 allowed a remote attacker to potentially execute arbitrary code inside the sandbox via a crafted HTML page. (Chromium security severity: Medium)

Vulnerabilities.Title: chromium-browser: Use after free in XML
Vulnerabilities.Description: Use after free in XML in Google Chrome prior to 148.0.7778.216 allowed a remote attacker to execute arbitrary code inside a sandbox via a crafted HTML page. (Chromium security severity: High)

Vulnerabilities.Title: libxslt: use-after-free with key data stored cross-RVT
Vulnerabilities.Description: A use-after-free vulnerability was found in libxslt while parsing xsl nodes that may lead to the dereference of expired pointers and application crash.

Vulnerabilities.Title: musl: musl: Arbitrary code execution via integer overflow in regcomp
Vulnerabilities.Description: musl libc before 1.2.7, when an untrusted regular expression is used with regcomp, has multiple integer overflows, possibly leading to incorrect allocation sizes and out-of-bounds heap writes.

Vulnerabilities.Title: musl: musl: Arbitrary code execution via integer overflow in regcomp
Vulnerabilities.Description: musl libc before 1.2.7, when an untrusted regular expression is used with regcomp, has multiple integer overflows, possibly leading to incorrect allocation sizes and out-of-bounds heap writes.

Vulnerabilities.Title: zlib: zlib: Heap buffer overflow in gz_vacate() allows arbitrary code execution
Vulnerabilities.Description: zlib 1.2.11 through 1.3.2 contains a heap buffer overflow: after an underlying write() fails, gz_write() returns without resetting strm.next_in, leaving it pointed at the caller's buffer. A later gz* write call then derives a position from the stale pointer and writes past a heap allocation; any write() failure reaches it, including EPIPE on a blocking descriptor, and in versions before 1.3.1.2 the failed write must be followed by a gzclearerr() call.

Vulnerabilities.Title: Improper Restriction of Operations within the Bounds of a Memory Buffe ...
Vulnerabilities.Description:
Improper Restriction of Operations within the Bounds of a Memory Buffer vulnerability in OSGeo gdal (frmts/zlib/contrib/infback9 modules). This vulnerability is associated with program files inftree9.C‎.

This issue affects gdal: before 3.11.0.
